taskDescription: Arrange the steps of vitamin D activation in the correct anatomical order, from synthesis to action.

sequenceImages.imageDescription: Skin: UV-B converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to vitamin D3
Intestine: calcitriol promotes calcium and phosphate absorption

l10n.score: You got @score of @total points. Vitamin D activation requires three organs in sequence — skin (UV-B photolysis), liver (25-hydroxylation) and kidney (1-alpha-hydroxylation) — so a block at any step (dark skin, liver disease or chronic kidney disease) can cause rickets or osteomalacia even when the upstream steps are intact.
